survey: A hexagonal wooden coffin stands upright on grass, turned three-quarters to the camera. It has two parts. The box is at the back: a back panel with side walls, and its right side wall shows as a thick plank edge. The lid is at the front: a flat hexagonal board with a raised cross, roughly facing the camera. The lid has been slid to the left, so a strip of padded purple lining shows in the gap along the right side, between the lid's edge and the box's side wall. The lid and the box both reach down to the grass. There are no hinges, latches, nails or anything else holding the lid to the box. The outlines match: the shoulder angles and the top and bottom edges of the lid line up with the box.

errors.where: Lid, the whole front panel against the upright box
errors.what: The coffin stands on its end, but the lid is shown slid sideways and ajar with no hinge, latch, nails or other support. Gravity cannot hold a lid against an upright box, so this lid, shifted half off, would fall forward. Nothing explains how it stays there.

errors.where: Purple lining in the right-hand gap between lid and box wall
errors.what: The lining bulges out through the gap, level with the lid's edge, as if it were a separate cushion pressed between lid and wall. It does not sit inside the box behind the lid. Lining should be fixed to the inside of the box and sit back from the opening.

fix: An upright wooden coffin with its lid fully closed and lined up with the box on all sides, held on by visible metal hinges along one side and nailed or latched shut. No gap and no lining visible. Or: the lid swung open on side hinges, with the purple satin lining visible inside the box.
